title: A Stellar–Solar Clock Model Linking Giza’s Plan, Chambers and Great Sphinx to Cygnus and the Galactic Centre
content: The completed Giza plan supplies a stellar–solar clock model whose younger fitted state lies near 2562 BCE, within the published 95% radiocarbon-based accession range for Khufu (2629–2558 BCE). The 12,400-year stellar search has no dynastic-age constraint. Under primary Vondrák precession, historical channels alone select 2594 BCE within the 68% range. Dimensionless ground invariants define paired angular targets separated by 57,600 years; the primary fit gives 0.166° RMS. Cygnus–Deneb–Galactic centre leads 504,400 fixed-star assignments and eight 440-model constellation panels with stellar motion. With Cygnus retained, full-sphere searches locate the reference 4.46 arcmin from Sagittarius A*, or 1.11 arcmin with measured reference motion. Target permutations preserve a unique sub-0.5° assignment. Broad integer freedom admits rivals; fixing the continuous terrestrial inclination retains the candidate as best located. Near 60,162 BCE, Cassiopeia reconstructs 24–28–34 at 0.175° RMS under propagated stellar motion. At the younger state, the solstitial Sun reproduces the register with 0.0171 code-unit residual. Material recovery extends to five chambers, the Queen’s niche and the Sphinx; four additional chambers fail the inherited rules. These retrospective mappings support a testable hypothesis that Giza’s architecture and sculpture represent celestial time, with a state compatible with Khufu’s era; ancient intention remains unresolved.
